text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
CAPITAL
- The State Ownership Fund has spent 10 billion lei in subsidising obscure newspapers, the weekly magazine says.
- Romania consumes three times less beer than countries in the European Union, says a report on output and consumption.
- Enterprises with high debts are to be liquidated this summer.
- The magazine publishes a report on the restructuring of the military industry.
- The privatisation of the energy sector is to end the state's monopoly. The state would control only the Cernavoda nuclear plant and several hydroelectric plants.
BURSA
- The prefect of the Transylvanian county of Cluj suspended construction authorisation for a McDonald's outlet in Cluj.
- The newspaper publishes a report on the underground economy drafted by the government's council for reform.
- Romania wants to attract international hotel chains to relaunch its tourism sector.
ADEVARUL
- Miners' wages should not rise to the disadvantage of other workers, said Matei Bratianu, leader of the one-million-strong National Union Bloc trade union.
- The deal between IAR helicopter producer and Bell helicopter is profitable for all partners, including the state, said FPS manager Sorin Dumitriu.
- Privatising the tabacco state authority Regia Autonoma a Tutunului would generate losses of hundreds of billions of lei.
- A two-week holiday on the Romanian Black Sea coast in miserable conditions costs almost as much as a holiday on the Canary Islands, says the newspaper.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romania to allocate two more licences for mobile GSM phones later this year.
- Coal miners in the western Jiu Valley continue their strike over demands of 45 percent pay rises.
General:
ADEVARUL
- The newspaper publishes a nine-point declaration drawn up by five "dissidents" from the former ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) urging the party to restructure.
- During debates on ratifying the Romanian-Ukrainian treaty, parliament is to adopt a declaration to explain certain of its points.
- Alexandru Safran, Geneva's Chief Rabbi and Romania's Chief Rabbi until he left the country in 1947, is to meet President Emil Constantinescu.
- The newspaper publishes a report on drug consumption in Romania.
- The newspaper publishes a report on the Romanian Orthodox Church and the Greek Catholic Church, following a dispute over restitution of some churches confiscated by the Communists.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The Romanian Intelligence Service (SRI) would return the manuscripts confiscated by the former Securitate to some 100 persons, said SRI manager Costin Georgescu.
NATIONAL
- On July 8, Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea may resign on health grounds and return to Bucharest city hall as mayor, sources say.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The government drafted a bill on a local referendum to be called over the recreation of 250 villages and 20 counties abolished by the communist regime.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The newspaper publishes an interview with former Reform Minsiter Mircea Cosea, member of the group of "dissidents" in the PDSR.
-- Bucharest Newsroom, 40-1 3120264
